title: r1 major QE: compile-failure modeled as a per-test kind; build-script and doctest surfaces unenumerated
description: Evidence: gate-data.md:11; contract line 64 keys wrong-reason on named-test identity + kind. Crate compile failure produces no per-test report entry — the kind cannot attach; doctests invert it (individually compiled, reported as failed doctests). Build-script failure is ambiguous between two lanes. Disposition: per_test vs whole_suite scope annotation on kinds, or move compile-failure to the cannot-run family keeping the doctest case; add build-script and doctest dispositions. Owner: solution-owner (kind vocabulary touches contract). Validator: quality-engineer.

comments.author: xqjG
comments.content: OPERATOR RULING (2026-07-21, round-1 triage): scope annotation on failure kinds. Each kind gains a per_test | whole_suite scope member; compile-failure is whole_suite (routing to the cannot-run family) EXCEPT doctests, where compile failure is genuinely per-test; build-script failure gets an explicit whole_suite disposition. Rejected: relocating compile-failure out of the enumeration (loses the doctest case's natural home). Amendment-class touch on the failure-kind text + data-side field addition at the fix pass.

comments.author: xqjG
comments.content: FIX LANDED (commit e61f28e5, gate-data 0.2.0): scope column (per-test | whole-suite) on every kind; doctest-compile-failure added as the per-test valid-red exception; build-script-failure added whole-suite routing to the cannot-run family; compile-failure marked whole-suite, conditional red retained. Schema encodes the scope enum and keeps exactly-one-conditional, now mechanically via contains. Contract touch rides #698. Round 2 re-verifies (validator: quality-engineer).
